subtheme: Regulated rate-base growth and utility buildout
metric_family: retail sales; customer counts; sector demand; balancing authority/state utility data
why_needed: Tests whether utility load-growth claims show up in delivered electricity, customers, or sector sales rather than only in forward-looking investor decks.
first_numbers_to_extract: annual retail sales by sector; customer counts; peak demand where available; utility service territory indicators
acceptance_rule: Accept only if the company utility can be mapped to EIA respondent/state/balancing-authority data and the period is explicit.
disproof_signal: Company claims rising load but EIA utility/state/sector data show flat or declining demand without a timing explanation.

subtheme: Regulated rate-base growth and utility buildout
outside_source: FERC Form 1 electric utility annual reports
metric_family: plant in service; construction work in progress; transmission plant; distribution plant; rate-base-adjacent financial data
why_needed: Tests whether utility capital plans are visible in regulatory financial accounts and whether capex is becoming plant rather than only forecast spend.
join_key: utility legal entity; FERC respondent; year
first_numbers_to_extract: electric plant in service; construction work in progress; transmission plant additions; distribution plant additions; accumulated depreciation
acceptance_rule: Accept only if FERC respondent maps cleanly to the company utility and table/line references are recorded.
disproof_signal: Investor deck says capital deployment is rising but FERC plant/CWIP additions do not support the direction or mix.

subtheme: Regulated rate-base growth and utility buildout
outside_source: FERC Form 714 balancing authority and planning area data
metric_family: hourly load; peak demand; planning-area demand
why_needed: Tests whether load-growth and reliability claims match actual balancing-authority/planning-area load patterns.
join_key: balancing authority; planning area; year; hour
first_numbers_to_extract: annual peak load; load duration indicators; hourly load growth; planning-area demand trend
acceptance_rule: Accept only if balancing authority or planning area can be tied to a named utility region or relevant service territory.
disproof_signal: Forward load claims are large but actual peak/load history gives no directional support and no timing bridge is disclosed.

outside_source: EIA Form EIA-860 detailed generator data
metric_family: generator capacity; planned additions; retirements; fuel type; ownership/operator
why_needed: Tests whether generation fleet scale, acquisitions, and planned capacity additions appear in plant-level capacity data.
join_key: plant; generator; operator; owner; fuel; county; year
first_numbers_to_extract: nameplate capacity; summer/winter capacity; planned generators; retirements; fuel mix; operating status
acceptance_rule: Accept only plant/generator rows with explicit company/operator/owner matching or documented asset-name crosswalk.
disproof_signal: Company claims capacity scarcity but EIA shows relevant owned/operator capacity declining or planned additions delayed without replacement explanation.

outside_source: EIA Form EIA-923 detailed generation and fuel data
metric_family: generation; fuel consumption; delivered fuel cost; plant utilization
why_needed: Tests whether owned/operated generation is actually producing power and whether fuel cost or utilization explains earnings.
first_numbers_to_extract: net generation; fuel consumption; fuel receipts; fuel cost; capacity factor proxy by plant/fuel
acceptance_rule: Accept only if EIA plant IDs can be linked to company assets or acquired fleets.
disproof_signal: Company monetization claim rests on scarce generation, but generation/utilization/fuel data do not support the claimed operating role.

metric_family: generation interconnection milestones; project status; projected commercial operation dates
why_needed: Tests Texas generation queues and BYOP/new-build claims against ERCOT project/milestone data.
join_key: project name; developer; county; fuel; MW; commercial operation date
first_numbers_to_extract: active projects; fuel type; MW; interconnection stage; projected COD; status changes
acceptance_rule: Accept only if project/developer/county/fuel/MW evidence reasonably matches the company-disclosed project.
disproof_signal: A BYOP/new-build claim has no matching ERCOT queue/project evidence or shows major delay/cancellation.

metric_family: interconnection queues; generator status; market data
why_needed: Tests Mid-Atlantic/Midwest capacity additions, retirements, and interconnection constraints against PJM public data.
join_key: queue ID; project name; zone; fuel; MW; status
first_numbers_to_extract: active queue MW; withdrawn projects; fuel mix; projected in-service dates; queue status changes
acceptance_rule: Accept only if queue/project identifiers and status dates are captured.
disproof_signal: Company-level contracted or development claims cannot be matched to queue status, or matched projects are withdrawn/delayed.

outside_source: EIA natural gas and liquids datasets/API
metric_family: natural gas production; flows; storage; NGL/LPG; exports; price series
why_needed: Tests ONEOK/Targa logistics growth against basin, NGL, LNG/export, and gas-market denominators.
first_numbers_to_extract: natural gas marketed production; NGL production; LPG exports; storage; regional price spreads where available
acceptance_rule: Accept only source series with stable series IDs, date coverage, units, and geographic/product definitions.
disproof_signal: Company volume/capex growth is not supported by basin/product/export denominator growth or is mostly price/mix rather than volume.

outside_source: Company quarterly and annual reports plus derived conversion table
metric_family: backlog conversion; revenue; EBITDA; operating cash flow; working capital; project charges
why_needed: Tests whether contractor backlog is converting into earnings and cash rather than only demand optics.
first_numbers_to_extract: beginning backlog; awards; revenue; gross margin; adjusted EBITDA; operating cash flow; working capital; project charges
acceptance_rule: Accept only if backlog/revenue/cash-flow periods align and segment definitions are stable or reconciled.
disproof_signal: Backlog rises but revenue, margin, or cash conversion deteriorates for multiple quarters without one-time explanation.

outside_source: Company annual/quarterly reports for ABM CACI and selected peers
metric_family: data-center; mission-critical; secure infrastructure; facility services; backlog; revenue exposure
why_needed: Tests whether digital infrastructure adjacency is a real disclosed revenue/backlog lane or just thematic proximity.
join_key: company; segment; customer vertical; quarter; year
first_numbers_to_extract: data-center revenue/backlog references; mission-critical facility services; secure infrastructure bookings; customer concentration; margin
acceptance_rule: Accept only explicit source-backed disclosures; do not infer data-center exposure from generic technology or facilities language.
disproof_signal: Adjacency companies do not disclose data-center/mission-critical/secure-infrastructure metrics, or exposure is immaterial/generic.

outside_source: State utility commission orders and rate cases
source_url: state commission dockets and utility IR pages
metric_family: approved capex; riders; customer contributions; allowed ROE; rate impacts
why_needed: Tests whether utility capital plans have legal/regulatory approval and how costs are allocated.
join_key: utility; state; docket; order date; project/rider
first_numbers_to_extract: approved revenue requirement; allowed ROE; capital tracker/rider; customer contribution; rate impact; settlement terms
acceptance_rule: Accept only docket/order-backed numbers with decision dates and affected utility.
disproof_signal: Company capital plan is reduced, deferred, rejected, or approved with returns/cost recovery materially below investor framing.

source_url: SEC filings; rating reports; lender releases; credit agreements
metric_family: debt financing; project finance; revolvers; term loans; tax equity; customer prepayments
why_needed: Tests who funds the buildout and whether capital comes from banks, bonds, private credit, project finance, customers, tax equity, or internal cash.
join_key: issuer/borrower; project; lender; facility; maturity; date
first_numbers_to_extract: facility size; lender group; use of proceeds; maturity; collateral; covenants; customer funding; tax-credit monetization
acceptance_rule: Accept only where financing document or rating/source note states use of proceeds and borrower/project relationship.
disproof_signal: Capital project exists but financing path is missing, unaffordable, covenant-constrained, or dependent on customer funding that is not secured.
